_: Which of two confusable components to reach for, and the condition under which the decision would be reopened. Authored; no library publishes this.

Checkbox ~ Switch.separated: when the change takes effect. A Switch acts the moment it is flipped and the screen must reflect it immediately; a Checkbox collects an answer that is submitted with the rest of the form. Both are two-state and look alike, which is why the wrong one is chosen so often.
Checkbox ~ Switch.reopenIf: the product adopts auto-saving forms, at which point the distinction stops being about timing and has to be redrawn.

Progress ~ Spinner.separated: whether the length is known. Progress needs a denominator; a Spinner is the honest answer when there is none. A Spinner shown for a task whose length IS known throws away information the user wants.
Progress ~ Spinner.reopenIf: Progress learns an indeterminate mode, which would make the pair one component with a prop.

Button ~ Link.separated: whether it acts or navigates, never how it looks. A Link that changes state breaks the back button and cannot be opened in a new tab meaningfully; a Button that navigates loses the address.
Button ~ Link.reopenIf: never — this one follows from the platform, not from this system.
